newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply down on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply down on liquidation.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended sharply lower on Friday on liquidation by major financial institutions ahead of the ending of the current reserve period on Saturday, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 6.809 against Thursday's 7.445 finish -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but far below the record double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper fell to 6.75 percent against 7.25.

Dealers said most financial institutions were busy in liquidating funds before the end of the current reserve period and the central bank's late-Thursday decision to raise two key interest rates did not have immediate impact on the market.
Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong announced a hike in the rediscount and secured loans rates by 0.25 percentage point.
He said the central bank would respect market forces in the forex market, but was determined to clamp down on speculation.

But on Friday, the Taiwan dollar sank anew to its lowest level since 1988 despite early speculative selling of greenbacks triggered by the central bank's decision to raise the two key interest rates, dealers said.
The local dollar closed at T$28.752 against Thursday's T$28.70, dealers said.
Dealers said they saw the money rates declining further on Saturday.
In the bond market, the 86/4 bond yield was traded at 6.1050 amid sluggish sentiment.
